claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the link target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers get long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page identifies which providers do.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) lists the current version of all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for scheduled automated drift detection and remediation.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name to form the physical name, and this allows replacement resources to be created before deleting the old resource.

Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack for encrypting secrets, configurable to use a custom secrets provider; encrypting the same value across two stacks yields different encrypted strings.
`pulumi config set --secret` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.

Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way, though some Pulumi providers use open-source Terraform schemas; Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are opt-in, enabled via a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, and can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pages exist at /docs/support/faq/secrets-config/, /docs/support/faq/pulumi-cloud/, /docs/support/faq/policies/, and /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship those patches.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Under the Pulumi provider support policy, exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a covered provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life on the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major version of a Pulumi provider, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider (recommended) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
Pinning to a specific major version is the recommended way to consume Pulumi provider LTS releases.
At any time, exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older majors receive no patches.
N is the latest released major version: if v3 is the newest release, v3 is N, v2 is N−1, and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major version (N) of a Pulumi provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
The LTS version (N−1) receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies, for up to 12 months from N's release or until N+1 ships.
Provider versions N−2 and older are end of life and not supported and will not receive updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what are the best practices for maintaining provider versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
